gallery.filename: Fort Boise showing interior buildings, Snake River near the mouth of the Boise River, Idaho, 1849 (AL+CA 1474).jpg
gallery.title: File:Fort Boise showing interior buildings, Snake River near the mouth of the Boise River, Idaho, 1849 (AL+CA 1474).jpg
gallery.description:
Picture of a color drawing by Major Osborne Cross.
Caption on image: Fort Boise on the Snake River Near the mouth of the Boise
This drawing is from the report of Major Osborne Cross to the Quarter Master General, August 29, 1849.  The Hudson Bay Company founded the fort in 1834 as a center for fur trading.  It later became a major stop on the Oregon Trail.  The fort was closed in 1855 due to flooding and attacks.
